dossier.architecture: Wide four-bar coral intake, compact elevator and separate algae collection.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; precise module specification not established by reviewed interview.
subsystems.intake: Wide four-bar folds inward under frontal impact. Composite plates and roller geometry were iterated; thicker carbon followed week-5 damage.
subsystems.transfer: Ground pickup feeds lightweight two-sided coral/algae end effector.
subsystems.scoring: Two-stage continuous string elevator; low carriage hardware and adjustable bracing reduce mass and top-stage wobble.
subsystems.endgame: Second major climber version adds guide wings, powered cage capture and latches; reported alignment/sequence improved from about 20 to 10 seconds.
subsystems.controls: Two Limelights for piece/pose detection and reef alignment; autonomous detection zones preserve partner compatibility.

versions: Climber version 2 recovers late-match cycling time. Algae floor-to-net use increased once alliances filled reefs faster.
dossier.analysis: The team explicitly identifies serviceability as a weakness: some intake changes took 30–45 minutes. A strategically attractive pickup can still be expensive to maintain, and that cost should be included when borrowing the mechanism.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2025-1678 · Wide pickup, light elevator and faster cage capture solve different delays
context_documents.body:
# 2025-1678: Wide pickup, light elevator and faster cage capture solve different delays

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A wide four-bar collector feeds the lightweight coral/algae effector on a string-driven continuous elevator. The interview describes thicker carbon after a week-five collector member bent and cracked; the caption does not safely establish the thickness. Later cage guides and capture wheels replace a slower alignment approach.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team links width to driver tolerance, elevator construction to speed/weight/CG, and the revised cage capture to reducing an approximately twenty-second climb process toward roughly ten seconds.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The motorized scoring cycle is only one part of match throughput. Wide acquisition can reduce driver correction, while a faster endgame can recover entire scoring cycles. Those gains can justify mass in guides or reinforcement even when they increase subsystem weight. The original and revised climb should not be averaged into one time, and the gain should not be applied to a team whose approach geometry differs.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure failed-pickup rate, full extension deflection and complete cage-approach-to-secured time. Repeat impact tests on the reinforced collector instead of assuming more carbon fixes every load direction.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/gUJUAoHRq8I](https://youtu.be/gUJUAoHRq8I)

source_reviews.title: Citrus Circuits robot history
facts: SubLime acquired both pieces, used elevator/end effector for all coral levels, scored algae in processor and net and climbed deep cage.

source_reviews.title: SubLime reveal
facts: Team unveiled SubLime ahead of three named regionals.
source_reviews.limitations: Reveal text provides version context more than construction.

source_reviews.title: Citrus Circuits Behind the Bumpers
source_reviews.review_basis: Read inherited synopsis. Full captions not retrieved.
facts: Prior account describes inward-folding four-bar intake, stage bracing, a revised cage grab and time-consuming intake service.
source_reviews.limitations: Detailed materials, service times and climb timing are inherited team accounts.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: SubLime pairs a wide coral collector with an elevator/end effector and an algae path. The floor intake’s capacity to accept an imperfect approach is useful only if the pipe reaches a repeatable loading pose. The older dossier identifies the operational cost of the intake as well as its intended collision behavior. A hard-to-replace collector can turn an isolated defense hit into lost practice or a compromised next match.
piece_flow: Floor coral enters the wide four-bar intake and is transferred to the coral side of the effector.
Elevator carries the effector to the reef. An algae intake and the opposite effector side support processor and net work.
The independent climb mechanism captures the deep cage after scoring.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: Retained notes describe a low carriage and adjustable stage bracing, plus inward collector motion under impact. The collapse path needs room between the bumper, chain or belt routes and guide plates. Check where the link stops under a real angled impact, because its compliant direction can change when one side hits first.

subsystems.name: Coral intake and transfer
subsystems.construction: Wide inward-folding four-bar with composite structure in retained synopsis.
subsystems.operation: Gather floor pipe and feed it toward the scoring carriage. Collapse inward under certain frontal contact.
subsystems.team_rationale: Older account reports thicker carbon after week-five damage and difficult intake service.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A stiffer plate can preserve roller alignment while shifting impact loads to fasteners and links. Compare both throughput and removal time after realistic damage.
subsystems.interfaces: Intake exit must match elevator loading height and heading. The collapse path competes with this transfer area.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test asymmetric impact and time complete intake extraction with all wiring installed.
subsystems.unknowns: Precise roller arrangement, materials and repair times by version.

subsystems.name: Elevator and dual-use scoring
subsystems.construction: Team confirms elevator and end effector. Two-stage continuous string and adjustable bracing are inherited.
subsystems.operation: Set the scoring height, with separate contacts for coral and algae.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team summary confirms algae destinations and four coral levels.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Low carriage mass can allow quicker motion, but lateral stage play projects to the piece. Match realistic drive acceleration and maximum extension when checking.
subsystems.interfaces: Shared vertical structure makes tip compliance common to both piece routes.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check string tension and bracing after a hard landing or cable fault.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact reeving, guide preload and release logic.

subsystems.name: Deep cage
subsystems.construction: Team confirms deep climb. Retained V2 account describes wings, powered capture and latches.
subsystems.operation: Guide the cage into capture and retain it while lifting.
subsystems.team_rationale: Prior dossier associates the revision with a shorter endgame sequence.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The range of usable approach poses may matter more than winch speed when endgame starts late. Compare acquisition and lifting separately.
subsystems.interfaces: Guide wings need clearance from the scoring hardware and partner approaches.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test failed first contact, bent wings and disable before full engagement.

revisions: Retained chronology records intake reinforcement before Worlds and V2 climber. Neither is assigned to every event.
transferable_principles: Measure service time and first-pass intake rate together.
Separate approach, engagement and lift when comparing climb cycle time.
disconfirming_conditions: A protected station strategy weakens the value of a complex wide intake.
Bracing that improves tip accuracy may make servicing more difficult.
remaining_gaps: Primary mechanical write-up or full captions, actual source file review and detailed revisions.

recommended_images.locator: Candidate frames showing intake side structure and V2 cage guides
